title.zh: 卷五 本紀第五: 海陵
title.raw: 卷五 本紀第五: 海陵 Volume 5 Annals 5: Hailing

sentences.zh: 廢帝海陵庶人亮，字元功，本諱迪古乃，遼王宗幹第二子也。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor Hailing the Commoner, Liang, style Yuangong, original taboo name Digunai, was the second son of Prince Lia Zonggan.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing—the deposed emperor and commoner whose taboo name was Liang—was styled Yuangong and had originally been taboo-named Digunai, the second son of Prince Lia Zonggan.

sentences.zh: 母大氏。

translations.literal: His mother was of the Da clan.
translations.idiomatic: His mother belonged to the Da clan.

sentences.zh: 天輔六年壬寅歲生。

translations.literal: He was born in the sixth year of Tianfu, the year renyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the sixth year of Tianfu (the renyin year).

sentences.zh: 天眷三年，年十八，以宗室子爲奉國上將軍，赴梁王宗弼軍前任使，以爲行軍萬戶，遷驃騎上將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjuan, at age eighteen, as an imperial clansman he was made General Who Supports the State, sent to Prince of Liang Zongbi’s army as envoy, named campaigning wanhu, and promoted to General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianjuan, at eighteen, he was named General Who Supports the State as a clansman, sent as envoy to Prince of Liang Zongbi’s army, made campaigning wanhu, and raised to General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，加龍虎衛上將軍，爲中京留守，遷光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong he was added General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, made regent of the Central Capital, and promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong year 4 he was made General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and regent of the Central Capital, and promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 爲人僄急，多猜忌，殘忍任數。

translations.literal: In person he was impetuous, full of suspicion, cruel, and scheming.
translations.idiomatic: He was impetuous, suspicious, cruel, and given to intrigue.

sentences.zh: 初，熙宗以太祖嫡孫嗣位，亮意以爲宗幹太祖長子，而己亦太祖孫，遂懷覬覦。

translations.literal: At first Xizong succeeded as Taizu’s legitimate grandson; Liang thought that Zonggan was Taizu’s eldest son and that he too was Taizu’s grandson, and so harbored ambition.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong took the throne as Taizu’s legitimate grandson, Liang reasoned that Zonggan was Taizu’s eldest son and that he himself was also Taizu’s grandson—and ambition took root.

sentences.zh: 在中京，專務立威，以厭伏小人。

translations.literal: In the Central Capital he devoted himself to establishing authority so as to cow petty men.
translations.idiomatic: At the Central Capital he made a point of ruling by fear to overawe the lowborn.

sentences.zh: 猛安蕭裕傾險敢決，亮結納之，每與論天下事。

translations.literal: The meng’an Xiao Yu was treacherous and bold in decision; Liang won him over and often discussed affairs of the realm with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu, a meng’an, was shrewd and bold; Liang drew him in and talked through the state with him again and again.

sentences.zh: 裕揣知其意，因勸海陵舉大事，語在《裕傳》。

translations.literal: Yu guessed his intent and therefore urged Hailing to undertake a great affair; the account is in Yu’s biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yu read his mind and pressed him to seize power; the story is told in Yu’s biography.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，召爲同判大宗正事，加特進。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year he was recalled as Associate Controller of the Imperial Clan Office and granted Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 7 he was recalled as associate controller of the imperial clan office and granted Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 十一月，拜尚書左丞，務攬持權柄，用其腹心爲省台要職，引蕭裕爲兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, strove to seize power, placed trusted men in key provincial and court posts, and brought in Xiao Yu as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he became left vice director of the Secretariat, worked to tighten his grip, put his intimates in key provincial and court posts, and installed Xiao Yu as vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 一日因召對，語及太祖創業艱難，亮因嗚咽流涕，熙宗以爲忠。

translations.literal: One day, summoned to audience, he spoke of the hardships of Taizu’s founding; Liang wept aloud, and Xizong took it for loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Once, called to audience, he spoke of how hard Taizu had won the realm; Liang broke into tears, and Xizong read it as devotion.

sentences.zh: 八年六月，拜平章政事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighth year he was appointed Councilor of State.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year 8 he was made councilor of state.

sentences.zh: 十一月，拜右丞相。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was appointed Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was made right chancellor.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，兼都元帥。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he was also made Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 9 he was also named commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 熙宗使小底大興國賜亮生日，悼后亦附賜禮物，熙宗不悅，杖興國百，追其賜物，海陵由此不自安。

translations.literal: Xizong sent the low attendant Daxingguo to give Liang birthday gifts; Empress Dowager Dao also sent gifts attached to his; Xizong was displeased, beat Daxingguo a hundred strokes, and reclaimed the gifts—Hailing was unsettled from this.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong sent the low attendant Daxingguo with birthday gifts for Liang; Empress Dowager Dao added gifts of her own. Xizong took offense, had Daxingguo beaten a hundred times, and took the gifts back. Hailing grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 三月，拜太保、領三省事，益邀求人譽，引用勢望子孫，結其歡心。

translations.literal: In the third month he was appointed Grand Preceptor and head of the Three Departments, sought people’s praise all the more, and employed descendants of powerful houses to win their goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was made grand preceptor and head of the three departments, courted reputation harder still, and brought in sons of great families to bind them to him.

sentences.zh: 四月，學士張鈞草詔忤旨死，熙宗問：「誰使爲之？

translations.literal: In the fourth month Academician Zhang Jun drafted an edict that offended the sovereign and died; Xizong asked: “Who had him do it?
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Academician Zhang Jun drafted an edict that offended the throne and was put to death. Xizong asked: “Who set him to it?

sentences.zh: 」左丞相宗賢對曰：「太保實然。

translations.literal: ” Left Chancellor Zongxian answered: “The Grand Preceptor indeed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Left Chancellor Zongxian said: “The grand preceptor, without doubt.

sentences.zh: 」熙宗不悅，遂出爲領行台尚書省事。

translations.literal: ” Xizong was displeased and sent him out as head of the mobile secretariat-chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xizong was angered and sent him out to head the mobile secretariat-chancellery.

sentences.zh: 過中京，與蕭裕定約而去。

translations.literal: Passing the Central Capital, he fixed a pact with Xiao Yu and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through the Central Capital, he sealed a pact with Xiao Yu and went on.

sentences.zh: 至良鄉，召還。

translations.literal: Reaching Liangxiang, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: At Liangxiang he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 海陵莫測所以召還之意，大恐。

translations.literal: Hailing could not fathom why he had been recalled and was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing could not guess why he was called back and was terrified.

sentences.zh: 既至，復爲平章政事，由是益危迫。

translations.literal: When he arrived he was again made Councilor of State, and from this felt all the more pressed.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was again made councilor of state—and felt the danger close in.

sentences.zh: 熙宗嘗以事杖左丞唐括辯及右丞相秉德，辯及與大理卿烏帶謀廢立，而烏帶先此謀告海陵。

translations.literal: Xizong had once beaten Left Vice Director Tangguo Bian and Right Chancellor Bingde over a matter; Bian and Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review Wudai plotted deposition, and Wudai had already informed Hailing of the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong had once beaten Tangguo Bian, left vice director, and Bingde, right chancellor, over some affair. Bian and Wudai, chief justice of the Court of Judicial Review, plotted to depose him; Wudai had already told Hailing.

sentences.zh: 他日，海陵與辯語及廢立事，曰：「若舉大事，誰可立者？

translations.literal: Another day Hailing spoke with Bian of deposition and said: “If we raise a great affair, whom can we enthrone?
translations.idiomatic: On another day Hailing spoke with Bian about removing the throne and asked: “If we raise a coup, whom should we set up?

sentences.zh: 」辯曰：「胙王常勝乎？

translations.literal: ” Bian said: “Is there not the Prince of Zu, Changsheng?
translations.idiomatic: ” Bian said: “What of the Prince of Zu, Changsheng?

sentences.zh: 」問其次，曰：「鄧王子阿懶。

translations.literal: ” Asked who came next, he said: “Prince of Deng’s son Aleng.
translations.idiomatic: ” Asked for the next choice, he said: “Aleng, son of the Prince of Deng.

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「阿懶屬疏，安得立？

translations.literal: ” Liang said: “Aleng’s line is remote—how can he be enthroned?
translations.idiomatic: ” Liang said: “Aleng is too far from the line—how could he rule?

sentences.zh: 」辯曰：「公豈有意邪？

translations.literal: ” Bian said: “Do you not yourself have intent?
translations.idiomatic: ” Bian said: “Surely you have someone else in mind?

sentences.zh: 」海陵曰：「果不得已，舍我其誰！

translations.literal: ” Hailing said: “If truly there is no choice, who but me!
translations.idiomatic: ” Hailing said: “If it must be done, who but me!

sentences.zh: 」于是旦夕相與密謀。

translations.literal: ” From then on they plotted together in secret day and night.
translations.idiomatic: ” From then on they plotted together in secret, day and night.

sentences.zh: 護衛將軍特思疑之，以告悼后曰：「辯等公餘每竊竊聚語，竊疑之。

translations.literal: Guard General Tesi suspected them and reported to Empress Dowager Dao: “Bian and the others, after hours, always gather and whisper in secret—I suspect them.
translations.idiomatic: Guard general Tesi grew suspicious and told Empress Dowager Dao: “Bian and the rest steal off after court and whisper together—I fear a plot.

sentences.zh: 」后以告熙宗。

translations.literal: ” The empress dowager told Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: ” The empress dowager told Xizong.

sentences.zh: 熙宗怒，召辯謂曰：「爾與亮謀何事，將如我何？

translations.literal: Xizong in anger summoned Bian and said: “What affair are you and Liang plotting—what do you mean to do to me?
translations.idiomatic: Xizong in anger summoned Bian and said: “What are you and Liang plotting—and what do you mean to do to me?

sentences.zh: 」杖之。

translations.literal: ” He had him beaten.
translations.idiomatic: ” He had him beaten.

sentences.zh: 亮因此忌常勝、阿懶，且惡特思。

translations.literal: Liang therefore resented Changsheng and Aleng and also hated Tesi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang therefore hated Changsheng and Aleng and loathed Tesi besides.

sentences.zh: 因河南兵士孫進自稱皇弟按察大王，而熙宗之弟止有常勝、查剌，海陵乘此構常勝、查剌、阿懶、達懶。

translations.literal: Because a soldier of the Henan army, Sun Jin, styled himself Younger Brother, Inspector King, and Xizong’s brothers were only Changsheng and Chaci, Hailing used this to frame Changsheng, Chaci, Aleng, and Taleng.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jin, a soldier of the Henan army, called himself Younger Brother, Inspector King—and Xizong had only Changsheng and Chaci as brothers—Hailing used the case to frame Changsheng, Chaci, Aleng, and Taleng.

sentences.zh: 熙宗使特思鞫之，無狀。

translations.literal: Xizong had Tesi interrogate them; no proof emerged.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong set Tesi to question them; nothing was proved.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「特思鞫不以實。

translations.literal: Hailing said: “Tesi’s interrogation did not get at the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said: “Tesi did not press the inquiry honestly.

sentences.zh: 」遂俱殺之。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon they were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Then they were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 護衛十人長僕散忽土舊受宗幹恩。

translations.literal: Guard ten-man captain Pusan Hutu had formerly received grace from Zonggan.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Hutu, captain of ten in the guard, had once owed Zonggan a debt of favor.

sentences.zh: 徒單阿里出虎與海陵姻家。

translations.literal: Tushan Alihuchu was tied to Hailing by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Tushan Alihuchu was kin to Hailing by marriage.

sentences.zh: 大興國給事寢殿，時時乘夜從主者取符鑰歸家，以爲常。

translations.literal: Daxingguo served in the sleeping quarters and would often at night take the tally and keys from the chief attendant home, as a matter of routine.
translations.idiomatic: Daxingguo attended the sleeping hall and often at night took the tally and keys from the chief attendant and carried them home as if it were nothing.

sentences.zh: 興國嘗以李老僧屬海陵，得爲尚書省令史，故使老僧結興國爲內應，而興國亦以被杖怨熙宗，遂與亮約。

translations.literal: Daxingguo had once asked Li Laoseng to recommend him to Hailing and thereby became a clerk in the Secretariat-Chancellery; he therefore had Laoseng win Daxingguo as an inside man, and Daxingguo, bearing a grudge from his beating, then joined in pact with Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Daxingguo had Li Laoseng speak for him to Hailing and won a clerkship in the secretariat-chancellery; he had Laoseng bind Daxingguo inside the palace, and Daxingguo, still smarting from the beating, made a pact with Liang.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁巳，忽土、阿里出虎內直。

translations.literal: On dingsi in the twelfth month Hutu and Alihuchu were on inner watch.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the twelfth month Hutu and Alihuchu held the inner watch.

sentences.zh: 是夜，興國取符鑰啟門納海陵、秉德、辯、烏帶、徒單貞、李老僧等人至寢殿，遂弑熙宗。

translations.literal: That night Daxingguo took the tally and keys, opened the gate, and admitted Hailing, Bingde, Bian, Wudai, Tushan Zhen, Li Laoseng, and others to the sleeping hall; they then assassinated Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: That night Daxingguo took the tally and keys, opened the gate, and let in Hailing, Bingde, Bian, Wudai, Tushan Zhen, Li Laoseng, and the rest to the sleeping hall—and killed Xizong.

sentences.zh: 秉德等未有所屬。

translations.literal: Bingde and the others had not yet settled on whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Bingde and the rest had not yet chosen whom to serve.

sentences.zh: 忽土曰：「始者議立平章，今復何疑。

translations.literal: Hutu said: “At the outset we discussed enthroning the Councilor of State—what doubt remains now?
translations.idiomatic: Hutu said: “We already agreed to make the councilor of state emperor—what is left to hesitate over?

sentences.zh: 」乃奉海陵坐，皆拜，稱萬歲。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon they raised Hailing to the seat; all bowed and shouted “Long live!”
translations.idiomatic: ” They seated Hailing on the throne; everyone bowed and cried “Long live the emperor!”

sentences.zh: 詐以熙宗欲議立后，召大臣，遂殺曹國王宗敏，左丞相宗賢。

translations.literal: Feigning that Xizong wished to discuss installing an empress, he summoned the great ministers and then killed Prince of Cao Guo Zongmin and left chief councillor Zongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Pretending Xizong meant to choose an empress, he called in the great ministers—and killed Prince Zongmin of Cao and Left Chief Councillor Zongxian.

sentences.zh: 是日，以秉德爲左丞相兼侍中、左副元帥，辯爲右丞相兼中書令，烏帶爲平章政事，忽土爲左副點檢，阿里出虎爲右副點檢，貞爲左衛將軍，興國爲廣甯尹。

translations.literal: That day Bingde was made left chief councillor and palace attendant and left vice commander-in-chief; Bian right chief councillor and director of the Secretariat; Wudai participating grand councilor; Hutu left vice director of palace inspection; Ali Chuhu right vice director of palace inspection; Zhen left guards general; Xingguo Guangning intendant.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Bingde became left chief councillor, palace attendant, and left vice commander-in-chief; Bian became right chief councillor and secretariat director; Wudai was named participating grand councilor; Hutu and Ali Chuhu were made left and right vice directors of palace inspection; Zhen became left guards general; and Xingguo became Guangning intendant.

sentences.zh: 于是自太師、領三省事勖以下二十人進爵增職各有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Grand Preceptor directing the Three Departments Xun downward, twenty men were advanced in noble rank and office, each to his degree.
translations.idiomatic: From Grand Preceptor Xun, who headed the Three Departments, through twenty more men, ranks and posts rose each according to merit.

sentences.zh: 己未，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiwei, a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 改皇統九年爲天德元年。

translations.literal: Huangtong year 9 was changed to Tiande year 1.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth year of Huangtong was renamed the first year of Tiande.

sentences.zh: 參知政事蕭肄除名。

translations.literal: Participating Grand Councilor Xiao Yi was stripped of his name and office.
translations.idiomatic: Participating Grand Councilor Xiao Yi was dismissed and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 鎮南統軍孛極爲尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Southern-route army commander Beji was made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Beji, commander of the southern-route army, was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 賜左丞相秉德、右丞相辯、平章政事烏帶、廣甯尹興國、點檢忽土、阿里出虎、左衛將軍貞、尚書省令史老僧、辯父刑部尚書阿里等錢絹馬牛羊有差。

translations.literal: Left chief councillor Bingde, right chief councillor Bian, participating grand councilor Wudai, Guangning intendant Xingguo, directors of inspection Hutu and Ali Chuhu, left guards general Zhen, Secretariat clerk Laoseng, and Bian’s father Minister of Punishments Ali were granted money, silk, horses, cattle, and sheep in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Bingde, Bian, Wudai, Xingguo, Hutu, Ali Chuhu, Zhen, Secretariat clerk Laoseng, and Bian’s father Ali of the Ministry of Punishments received cash, silk, horses, cattle, and sheep in set measures.

sentences.zh: 甲子，誓太祖廟，召秉德、辯、烏帶、忽土、阿里出虎、興國六人賜誓券。

translations.literal: On jiazi they swore oath at Taizu’s temple and summoned Bingde, Bian, Wudai, Hutu, Ali Chuhu, and Xingguo—six men—and bestowed oath certificates.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the six—Bingde, Bian, Wudai, Hutu, Ali Chuhu, and Xingguo—took oath at Taizu’s temple and received written pledge bonds.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以燕京路都轉運使劉麟爲參知政事。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Yanjing Route transport commissioner Liu Lin was made participating grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Liu Lin, transport commissioner of the Yanjing Route, was appointed participating grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，太傳、領三省事蕭仲恭，尚書右丞稟罷。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Grand Preceptor directing the Three Departments Xiao Zhonggong and right vice director Bing were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou Grand Preceptor Xiao Zhonggong, who headed the Three Departments, and Right Vice Director Bing were removed.

sentences.zh: 以行台尚書左丞溫都思忠爲右丞。

translations.literal: Mobile secretariat left vice director Wendusi Zhong was made right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Wendusi Zhong, left vice director on the mobile secretariat, was promoted to right vice director.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，追諡皇考太師憲古弘道文昭武烈章孝睿明皇帝，廟號德宗，名其故居曰興聖宮。

translations.literal: On yihai, the deceased father was posthumously titled Grand Preceptor, Ancient-in-Statutes Vast-in-the-Way Illustrious-in-Culture Martial-and-Ardent Discerning-in-Filial Piety Sagacious-and-Bright Emperor, with temple name Dezong; his former residence was named the Palace of Sagely Ascent.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Hailing posthumously enfeoffed his father as Grand Preceptor and emperor under the style Ancient in Statutes, Vast in the Way, Illustrious in Culture, Martial and Ardent, Discerning in Filial Piety, Sagacious and Bright—temple name Dezong—and named his old house the Palace of Sagely Ascent.

sentences.zh: 宋、高麗、夏賀正旦使中道遣還。

translations.literal: Envoys from Song, Goryeo, and Xia congratulating on New Year’s Day were sent back on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Song, Goryeo, and Xia envoys bound for the New Year audience were turned back mid-journey.

sentences.zh: 二年正月辛巳，以同知中京留守事蕭裕爲秘書監。

translations.literal: In the second year, first month, on xinsi, associate Central Capital intendant Xiao Yu was made director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Tiande year 2, first month, xinsi: Xiao Yu, deputy Central Capital intendant, became director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，尊嫡母徒單氏及母大氏皆爲皇太后。

translations.literal: On guisi, the stepmother of the Tushan clan and the mother of the Da clan were both honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi both his stepmother of the Tushan clan and his mother of the Da clan were raised to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 名徒單氏宮曰永壽，大氏宮曰永寧。

translations.literal: The Tushan palace was named Everlasting Longevity; the Da palace Everlasting Peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Tushan empress dowager’s residence was called Everlasting Longevity; the Da empress dowager’s, Everlasting Peace.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以勵官守、務農時、慎刑罰、揚側陋、恤窮民、節財用、審才實七事詔中外。

translations.literal: On yisi, an edict to court and realm set forth seven matters: encourage official integrity, attend to farming seasons, be careful with punishments, elevate obscure talent, pity the destitute, economize spending, and examine real ability.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi an edict to the empire urged seven things: hold office faithfully, keep to the farming calendar, punish with care, lift hidden worthies, relieve the poor, husband state funds, and weigh men by true merit.

sentences.zh: 遣侍衛親步軍都指揮使完顏思恭等以廢立事報諭宋、高麗、夏國。

translations.literal: Personal Guards and Step-Army commander-in-chief Wanyan Sigong and others were sent to report the deposition and enthronement to Song, Goryeo, and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Sigong, commander of the personal guards and step army, and others were dispatched to inform Song, Goryeo, and Xia of the coup.

sentences.zh: 以左丞相兼左副元帥秉德領行台尚書省事。

translations.literal: Left chief councillor and left vice commander-in-chief Bingde was ordered to head mobile secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bingde, left chief councillor and left vice commander-in-chief, was put in charge of the mobile secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二月戊申朔，封子元壽爲崇王。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wushen, the new-moon day, his son Yuanshou was enfeoffed as Prince of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, new moon wushen: his son Yuanshou was made prince of Chong.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，降前帝爲東昏王。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the former emperor was demoted to Prince of Eastern Darkness.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the deposed sovereign was reduced to prince of Eastern Darkness.

sentences.zh: 給天水郡公孫女二人月俸。

translations.literal: Two granddaughters of the Duke of Tianshui were granted monthly stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Two granddaughters of the duke of Tianshui were given monthly rations.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以兵部尚書完顏元宜等充賀宋生日使。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Minister of War Wanyan Yuanyi and others were appointed envoys to congratulate Song on the emperor’s birthday.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Wanyan Yuanyi of the Ministry of War and others were named envoys to Song for the emperor’s birthday.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，群臣上尊號曰法天膺運睿武宣文大明聖孝皇帝，詔中外。

translations.literal: On wuchen the ministers offered the honorific Aligning with Heaven, Receiving the Mandate, Sagaciously Martial, Propagating Culture, Greatly Illumined, Sacredly Filial Emperor; an edict announced this within and without.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the court offered the style Aligning with Heaven, Receiving the Mandate, Sagaciously Martial, Propagating Culture, Greatly Illumined, Sacredly Filial Emperor, and proclaimed it at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 永壽、永甯兩太后父祖贈官有差。

translations.literal: The fathers and grandfathers of the two empress dowagers of Everlasting Longevity and Everlasting Peace were granted offices in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers and grandfathers of the Everlasting Longevity and Everlasting Peace empress dowagers received posthumous offices, each to his measure.

sentences.zh: 以右丞相唐括辯爲左丞相，平章政事烏帶爲右丞相。

translations.literal: Right chief councillor Tangguo Bian was made left chief councillor; participating grand councilor Wudai was made right chief councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Tangguo Bian moved from right to left chief councillor, and participating grand councilor Wudai became right chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 三月丙戌，宋、高麗遣使賀即位。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingxu, Song and Goryeo sent envoys congratulating his enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, bingxu: Song and Goryeo sent envoys to hail the new reign.

sentences.zh: 以弟袞爲司徒兼都元帥。

translations.literal: His younger brother Gun was made Minister of Education and commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Gun was named minister of education and commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 詔以天水郡王玉帶歸宋。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the jade belt of the Prince of Tianshui returned to Song.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent the prince of Tianshui’s jade belt back to Song.

sentences.zh: 四月戊午，殺太傅、領三省事宗本，尚書左丞相唐括辯，判大宗正府事宗美。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, on wuwu, Grand Preceptor directing the Three Departments Zongben, left chief councillor Tangguo Bian, and chief judge of the Imperial Clan Court Zongmei were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, wuwu: Grand Preceptor Zongben, left chief councillor Tangguo Bian, and imperial-clan chief judge Zongmei were executed.

sentences.zh: 遣使殺領行台尚書省事秉德，東京留守宗懿，北京留守卞及太宗子孫七十余人，周宋國王宗翰子孫三十余人，諸宗室五十餘人。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to kill Bingde, who headed mobile secretariat affairs; Eastern Capital intendant Zongyi; Beijing intendant Bian; more than seventy descendants of Taizong; more than thirty descendants of Zhou-Song Prince of State Zonghan; and more than fifty members of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Agents were sent to kill Bingde at the mobile secretariat, Zongyi at the Eastern Capital, Bian at Beijing, seventy-odd of Taizong’s line, thirty-odd of Prince Zonghan’s house, and fifty-odd clansmen besides.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以尚書省譯史蕭玉爲禮部尚書，秘書監蕭裕爲尚書左丞，司徒袞領三省事、封王，都元帥如故，右丞相烏帶司空、左丞相兼侍中，平章政事劉筈爲尚書右丞相兼中書令，左丞宗義，右丞溫都思忠爲平章政事，參知政事劉麟爲尚書右丞，殿前左副點檢僕散忽土爲殿前都點檢。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Secretariat translator Xiao Yu was made Minister of Rites; Palace Library director Xiao Yu was made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs; Minister of Education Gun headed the Three Departments and was enfeoffed as prince, commander-in-chief unchanged; right chief councillor Wudai was made Minister of Works and left chief councillor and palace attendant; participating grand councilor Liu Ke was made right chief councillor and director of the Secretariat; left vice director Zongyi and right vice director Wendusi Zhong were made participating grand councilors; participating grand councilor Liu Lin was made right vice director; left vice director of palace inspection Pusan Hutu was made director of palace inspection.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the translator Xiao Yu became minister of rites and the library director Xiao Yu left vice director; Gun kept command but was made prince and head of the Three Departments; Wudai became minister of works and left chief councillor; Liu Ke became right chief councillor and secretariat director; Zongyi and Wendusi Zhong became participating grand councilors; Liu Lin became right vice director; and Pusan Hutu, left vice director of inspection, became director of inspection.

sentences.zh: 五月戊子，以平章行台尚書省事、右副元帥大抃爲行台尚書右丞相，元帥如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on wuzi, participating grand councilor of mobile secretariat affairs and right vice commander-in-chief Da Ban was made right chief councillor of the mobile secretariat, commander-in-chief unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, wuzi: Da Ban, participating grand councilor on the mobile secretariat and right vice commander-in-chief, became its right chief councillor while keeping command.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以左副元帥撒離喝爲行台尚書左丞相，元帥如故。

translations.literal: On renchen, left vice commander-in-chief Salih was made left chief councillor of the mobile secretariat, commander-in-chief unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Salih, left vice commander-in-chief, became left chief councillor of the mobile secretariat without losing command.

sentences.zh: 同判大宗正事宗安爲御史大夫。

translations.literal: Associate chief judge of the Imperial Clan Court Zongan was made censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zongan, associate head of the imperial-clan court, was named censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 六月丙午朔，高麗遣使賀即位。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingwu, the new-moon day, Goryeo sent envoys congratulating his enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, new moon bingwu: Goryeo sent envoys to hail the new reign.

sentences.zh: 甲子，太廟初設四神門及四隅罘罳。

translations.literal: On jiazi the ancestral temple first received Four Spirit Gates and corner spirit-screens.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the ancestral temple was fitted for the first time with Four Spirit Gates and corner awnings.

sentences.zh: 九月甲午，立惠妃徒單氏爲皇后。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiawu, Consort Tushan was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, jiawu: Consort Tushan of the Tushan clan was made empress.

sentences.zh: 十月癸卯，太師、領三省事勖致仕。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on guimao, Grand Preceptor directing the Three Departments Xun retired.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, guimao: Grand Preceptor Xun, who headed the Three Departments, left office.

sentences.zh: 辛未，殺太皇太妃蕭氏及其子任王偎喝。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Grand Empress Dowager Xiao and her son Prince Ren Weihai were killed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Grand Empress Dowager Xiao and her son, Prince Ren Weihai, were put to death.

sentences.zh: 使使殺行台左丞相、左副元帥撒離喝于汴，並殺平章政事宗義、前工部尚書謀里野、御史大夫宗安，皆夷其族。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to kill mobile secretariat left chief councillor and left vice commander-in-chief Salih at Bian, and to kill participating grand councilor Zongyi, former Minister of Works Moliye, and censor-in-chief Zongan—all their clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Agents killed Salih at Bian and executed participating grand councilor Zongyi, former minister of works Moliye, and censor-in-chief Zongan, exterminating every clan to the last.

sentences.zh: 以魏王斡帶之孫活里甲好修飾，亦族之。

translations.literal: Huolijia, grandson of Prince Wei Wandai, was fond of adornment; his whole clan was exterminated as well.
translations.idiomatic: Huolijia, a grandson of Prince Wei Wandai, loved finery—so his entire house was wiped out too.

sentences.zh: 十一月癸未，尚書右丞相劉筈罷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on guiwei, right chief councillor Liu Ke was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, guiwei: Right Chief Councillor Liu Ke was removed.

sentences.zh: 以會甯牧徒單恭爲平章政事。

translations.literal: Huining herdsman Tushan Gong was made participating grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Tushan Gong, herdsman of Huining, was appointed participating grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞劉麟、右丞完顏思恭罷。

translations.literal: Left vice director Liu Lin and right vice director Wanyan Sigong were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Liu Lin and Right Vice Director Wanyan Sigong were removed.

sentences.zh: 以參知政事張浩爲尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Participating Grand Councilor Zhang Hao was made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Participating Grand Councilor Zhang Hao became right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以行台尚書左丞張通古爲尚書左丞。

translations.literal: On yiyou, mobile secretariat left vice director Zhang Tonggu was made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Zhang Tonggu, left vice director on the mobile secretariat, became left vice director at the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，白虹貫日。

translations.literal: On bingxu a white rainbow spanned the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu a white rainbow cut across the sun.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以太后旨稱令旨。

translations.literal: On dinghai, edicts issued in the empress dowager’s name were styled lingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai rescripts in the empress dowager’s name were called command-edicts (lingzhi).

sentences.zh: 戊子，以十二事戒約官吏。

translations.literal: On wuzi, twelve injunctions were promulgated to warn and bind officials.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the court issued twelve admonitions binding officials to their duty.

sentences.zh: 己丑，命庶官許求次室二人，百姓亦許置妾。

translations.literal: On jichou, common officials were permitted to take two secondary wives, and commoners were also permitted to keep concubines.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou common officials were allowed two secondary wives, and commoners too were permitted concubines.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸卯朔，詔去群臣所上尊號。

translations.literal: On guimao, first day of the twelfth month, an edict removed the honorific titles the officials had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, the twelfth month’s new moon, an edict stripped away the honorifics the court had heaped on the throne.

sentences.zh: 丙午，初定襲封衍聖公俸格。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the salary scale for the hereditary Duke Yansheng was first fixed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the stipend for the hereditary Duke Yansheng was set for the first time.

sentences.zh: 命外官去所屬百里外者不許參謁，百里內者往還不得過三日。

translations.literal: It was ordered that outer officials who were more than a hundred li from their post might not come to audience, and those within a hundred li might not be away on the round trip for more than three days.
translations.idiomatic: An order barred outer officials stationed beyond a hundred li from traveling in for audience; those within a hundred li could not be gone more than three days on the journey there and back.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，立太祖射碑于紇石烈部中，上及皇后致奠于碑下。

translations.literal: On guichou, Taizu’s shooting stele was erected among the Hesheli tribe; the emperor and empress offered libations below the stele.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Taizu’s archery stele was raised among the Hesheli; the emperor and empress poured offerings at its foot.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，野人來獻異香，卻之。

translations.literal: On jiayin, wild tribesmen presented exotic incense; it was declined.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin forest people brought rare incense; the court refused it.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，有司奏慶雲見，上曰：「朕何德以當此。

translations.literal: On yimao, the authorities reported that auspicious clouds had appeared. The emperor said: “What virtue have I that deserves this?
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the ministries reported auspicious clouds. The emperor said, “What virtue is in me, that heaven should send this?

sentences.zh: 自今瑞應毋得上聞，若有妖異，當以諭朕，使自警焉。

translations.literal: From now on auspicious omens are not to be reported upward; if there are strange or ill portents, you should inform me so that I may take warning.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter do not report lucky signs to me. If there is anything ominous, tell me at once, that I may guard myself.

sentences.zh: 」己未，罷行台尚書省。

translations.literal: ”On jiwei, the Mobile Branch Secretariat was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: ”On jiwei the mobile branch secretariat was abolished.

sentences.zh: 改都元帥府爲樞密院。

translations.literal: The Supreme Marshalate was changed to the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme marshalate became the privy council.

sentences.zh: 詔改定繼絕法。

translations.literal: An edict revised the law on continuing extinct lineages.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reworked the rules for adopting heirs to continue a cut-off line.

sentences.zh: 以右副元帥大抃爲尚書右丞相兼中書令，參知行台尚書省事張中孚爲參知政事，都元帥袞爲樞密使，太尉、領三省事如故，元帥左監軍昂爲樞密副使，刑部尚書趙資福爲御史大夫。

translations.literal: Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Da Fen was made right chief councillor of the Secretariat and concurrently Zhongshu director; Zhang Zhongfu, who administered mobile-branch secretariat affairs as participation councillor, was made participation councillor; Supreme Commander Gun was made privy commissioner; the Grand Preceptor continued to head the Three Departments as before; Left Army Supervisor Ang was made vice privy commissioner; Minister of Punishments Zhao Zifu was made censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Right deputy commander-in-chief Da Fen became right chief councillor of the secretariat and director of the Zhongshu office; Zhang Zhongfu, who had run mobile-branch secretariat business as participation councillor, was made participation councillor; supreme commander Gun became privy commissioner; the grand preceptor still headed the Three Departments; left army supervisor Ang became vice privy commissioner; Minister of Punishments Zhao Zifu became censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 三年正月癸酉朔，宋、夏、高麗遣使來賀。

translations.literal: Third year, first month, on guiyou, new-moon day, Song, Xia, and Goryeo sent envoys to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on guiyou, the first month’s new moon, Song, Western Xia, and Goryeo sent New Year envoys.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，參知政事蕭玉丁憂，起復如故。

translations.literal: On yihai, Participation Councillor Xiao Yu entered mourning for a parent but was recalled to office as before.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai participation councillor Xiao Yu went into mourning, yet was recalled to his post without leave.

sentences.zh: 癸未，立春，觀擊土牛。

translations.literal: On guiwei, at the Beginning of Spring, he watched the striking of the clay ox.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, at the Beginning of Spring, he watched the ritual beating of the clay ox.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，初造燈山于宮中。

translations.literal: On dinghai, for the first time lamp mountains were built in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai lamp mountains were erected in the palace for the first time.

sentences.zh: 戊子，生辰，宋、高麗、夏遣使來賀。

translations.literal: On wuzi, his birthday; Song, Goryeo, and Xia sent envoys to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, his birthday, Song, Goryeo, and Western Xia sent congratulatory envoys.

sentences.zh: 甲午，初置國子監。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the Directorate of Education was first established.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the Directorate of Education was founded.

sentences.zh: 謂御史大夫趙資福曰：「汝等多徇私情，未聞有所彈劾，朕甚不取。

translations.literal: He said to Censor-in-Chief Zhao Zifu: “You and the rest show too much partiality in private matters, and I have not heard that you impeach anyone—I deeply disapprove.
translations.idiomatic: He told Censor-in-Chief Zhao Zifu, “You favor your friends and seldom bring charges—I want none of that.

sentences.zh: 自今百官有不法者，必當舉劾，無憚權貴。

translations.literal: From now on, whenever any official acts unlawfully, you must impeach him and not fear the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: From this day, any official who breaks the law must be impeached, without fear of the mighty.

sentences.zh: 」乙未，上出獵，宰相以下辭于近郊。

translations.literal: ”On yiwei, the emperor went out hunting; the chief ministers and below took leave at the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: ”On yiwei the emperor rode out to hunt; the chief ministers and those below bade him farewell at the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 上駐馬戒之曰：「朕不惜高爵厚祿以任汝等，比聞事多留滯，豈汝等苟圖自安不以民事爲念耶？

translations.literal: He reined in his horse and warned them: “I do not begrudge high rank and thick salary in appointing you, yet I hear that affairs are much delayed—do you seek only your own ease and not think of the people’s business?
translations.idiomatic: Halting his horse he admonished them: “I give you high rank and rich stipends without stint, yet I hear cases stall for days—are you only saving yourselves and not minding the people’s affairs?

sentences.zh: 自今朕將察其勤惰，以爲賞罰，其各勉之。

translations.literal: From now on I shall examine your diligence and slackness and use them for reward and punishment; each of you must exert himself.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth I will watch who is diligent and who is lax, and reward or punish accordingly. Do your utmost.

sentences.zh: 」丁酉，白虹貫日。

translations.literal: ”On dingyou, a white rainbow crossed the sun.
translations.idiomatic: ”On dingyou a white rainbow cut across the sun.

sentences.zh: 二月丁巳，還宮。

translations.literal: Second month, on dingsi, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingsi, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 三月庚寅，以翰林學士劉長言等爲宋生日使。

translations.literal: Third month, on gengyin, Hanlin academicians Liu Changyan and others were made envoys for Song’s imperial birthday.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengyin, Hanlin academicians Liu Changyan and others were sent as envoys for the Song emperor’s birthday.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，詔廣燕城，建宮室。

translations.literal: On renchen, an edict ordered Yanjing enlarged and palaces built.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen an edict commanded the widening of Yanjing and the raising of palace halls.

sentences.zh: 己亥，謂侍臣曰：「昨太子生日，皇后獻朕一物，大是珍異，卿試觀之。

translations.literal: On jihai he said to his attendants: “Yesterday, on the crown prince’s birthday, the empress gave me a gift most rare and strange—look at it.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he told his attendants, “Yesterday, the crown prince’s birthday, the empress gave me something most curious—see what you make of it.

sentences.zh: 」即出諸絳囊中，乃田家稼穡圓。

translations.literal: ”He then took it from a crimson silk pouch: it was a round painting of farming in a peasant household.
translations.idiomatic: ”He drew it from a crimson pouch: a round scene of a farm family at their planting.

sentences.zh: 「后意太子生深宮之中，不知民間稼穡之艱難，故以爲獻，朕甚賢之。

translations.literal: “The empress meant that the crown prince was born deep in the palace and does not know the hardship of farming among the people, and so offered this. I think her most worthy.”
translations.idiomatic: “The empress meant that a boy raised in the inner quarters cannot know how hard the fields are for common folk—that is why she gave this. I hold her in high esteem.”

sentences.zh: 」四月丙午，詔遷都燕京。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on bingwu, an edict ordered the capital moved to Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on bingwu, an edict ordered the capital transferred to Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，有司圖上燕城宮室制度，營建陰陽五姓所宜。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the authorities submitted plans of the Yanjing palace layout and what the five elements and yin-yang deemed auspicious for construction.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the ministries presented plans for the Yanjing palaces and the geomancers’ verdict on auspicious siting.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「國家吉凶，在德不在地。

translations.literal: Hailing said: “A state’s fortune or ruin lies in virtue, not in the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, “Whether a realm thrives or falls is a matter of virtue, not of soil.

sentences.zh: 使桀、紂居之，雖卜善地何益。

translations.literal: If Jie and Zhou lived there, what good would divining a lucky site do?
translations.idiomatic: Set Jie and Zhou on the finest ground—what would divination avail?

sentences.zh: 使堯、舜居之，何用卜爲。

translations.literal: If Yao and Shun lived there, why need divination at all?”
translations.idiomatic: Set Yao and Shun anywhere—why bother to divine?”

sentences.zh: 」丙寅，罷歲貢鷹隼。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the annual tribute of hawks and falcons was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the yearly tribute of hawks and falcons was ended.

sentences.zh: 沂州男子吳真犯法，當死，有司以其母老疾無侍爲請，命官與養濟，著爲令。

translations.literal: A man of Yizhou, Wu Zhen, broke the law and deserved death; the authorities pleaded that his mother was old and ill with no one to serve her. He was ordered given official support and care, and this was written into statute.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhen of Yizhou had committed a capital crime; the courts pleaded that his mother was aged and ill and had no one to tend her. The emperor ordered him supported at public expense and made the rule permanent.

sentences.zh: 閏月辛未朔，命尚書右丞張浩調選燕京，仍諭浩無私徇。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, on xinwei, new-moon day, Right Vice Director Zhang Hao was ordered to conduct selections at Yanjing, and Hao was instructed not to show private favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on xinwei, the new moon, Right Vice Director Zhang Hao was sent to run appointments at Yanjing and warned against favoritism.

sentences.zh: 丙子，命太官常膳惟進魚肉，舊貢鵝鴨等悉罷之。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the Imperial Kitchen’s regular meals were to serve only fish and meat; the old tribute of geese, ducks, and the like was all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the imperial kitchen was limited to fish and meat for daily fare; tribute geese, ducks, and such were all stopped.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，罷皇統間苑中所養禽獸。

translations.literal: On dingchou, the birds and beasts kept in the parks during Huangtong were all released.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the birds and beasts penned in the parks since Huangtong were set free.

sentences.zh: 歸德軍節度使阿魯補以撤官舍材木構私第，賜死。

translations.literal: Guide Army military commissioner Alubu used timber stripped from government buildings to build a private residence and was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Alubu, military commissioner of the Guide Army, had stripped official buildings for timber to build his own house and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，詔朝官稱疾不治事者，尚書省令監察御史與太醫同診視，無實者坐之。

translations.literal: On wuxu, an edict ruled that court officials who claimed illness and neglected their duties were to be examined jointly by the Secretariat and the surveillance censor together with the imperial physicians; those found feigning were punished.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu an edict required that officials who pleaded sickness and shirked duty be diagnosed by the secretariat, a surveillance censor, and the court physicians together; sham illness was penalized.

sentences.zh: 五月壬子，以戒敕宰相以下官，詔中外。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on renzi, he admonished the chief ministers and officials below, and an edict announced this inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renzi, he lectured the chief ministers and the ranks below, and an edict carried his words through the realm.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，宰臣請益嬪御以廣嗣續。

translations.literal: On wuchen, the chief ministers asked that more consorts be taken to broaden the imperial line.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the chief ministers asked that more consorts be taken, that the line might continue.

sentences.zh: 上命徒單貞語宰臣，前所誅党人諸婦人中多朕中表親，欲納之官中。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Tudan Zhen to tell the chief ministers: “Among the women of the faction we executed, many are my cousins by marriage; I wish to take them into the palace.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Tudan Zhen tell the ministers, “Of the wives left from the men we killed, many are my kin by marriage. I mean to bring them into the palace.”

sentences.zh: 平章政事蕭裕不可，上不從。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Xiao Yu objected; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Chief councillor Xiao Yu protested; the emperor would not hear him.

sentences.zh: 遂納宗本子莎魯啜，宗固子胡里剌、胡失打，秉德弟糺里等妻宮中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took into the palace Zongben’s son’s wife Shaluchuo, Zonggu’s sons’ wives Hulila and Hushida, and Bingde’s younger brother Jiuli’s wife.
translations.idiomatic: He then took into the palace Shaluchuo, wife of Zongben’s son; Hulila and Hushida, wives of Zonggu’s sons; and the wife of Bingde’s younger brother Jiuli.

sentences.zh: 六月丙子，殺太府監完顏馮六。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on bingzi, Director of the Imperial Storehouse Wanyan Fengliu was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingzi, Director of the Imperial Storehouse Wanyan Fengliu was executed.

sentences.zh: 宋遣使祈請山陵，不許。

translations.literal: Song sent envoys to petition for repair of the imperial tombs; permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Song sent envoys begging leave to tend the imperial tombs; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 九月庚戌，賜燕京役夫帛，人一匹。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on gengxu, cloth was bestowed on Yanjing corvée laborers, one bolt per man.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengxu, each corvée worker at Yanjing received one bolt of cloth.

sentences.zh: 以東京路兵馬都總管府判官蕭子敏爲高麗生日使，修起居注蕭彭哥爲夏國生日使。

translations.literal: Xiao Zimin, judicial intendant of the Eastern Capital Route army-and-horse headquarters, was made birthday envoy to Goryeo; Xiao Pengge, reviser of the Diary of Activity, was made birthday envoy to Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zimin, judicial intendant on the Eastern Capital Route staff, was sent as birthday envoy to Goryeo; Xiao Pengge, reviser of the Diary of Activity, as birthday envoy to Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 四年正月丁酉朔，宋、高麗、夏遣使來賀。

translations.literal: Fourth year, first month, on dingyou, new-moon day, Song, Goryeo, and Xia sent envoys to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, on dingyou, the first month’s new moon, Song, Goryeo, and Western Xia sent New Year envoys.

sentences.zh: 群臣請立皇太子，從之。

translations.literal: The ministers asked to establish a crown prince; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers asked that a crown prince be named; the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，初定東宮官屬。

translations.literal: On wuxu the Eastern Palace staff was first defined.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the offices of the Eastern Palace were set down for the first time.

sentences.zh: 立捕盜賞格。

translations.literal: Rewards for capturing bandits were set by regulation.
translations.idiomatic: A bounty schedule for captured bandits was promulgated.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，太白經天。

translations.literal: On guimao, Venus crossed the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Venus crossed the sky—an omen.

sentences.zh: 壬子，生辰，宋、高麗、夏遣使來賀。

translations.literal: On renzi, his birthday; Song, Goryeo, and Xia sent envoys to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, his birthday, Song, Goryeo, and Western Xia sent congratulatory envoys.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，朝謁世祖、太祖、太宗、德宗陵。

translations.literal: On guihai he performed court worship at the tombs of Shizu, Taizu, Taizong, and Dezong.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai he went in state to worship at the tombs of Shizu, Taizu, Taizong, and Dezong.

sentences.zh: 甲子，還宮。

translations.literal: On jiazi he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 二月丁卯，立子光英爲皇太子，庚午，詔中外。

translations.literal: Second month, on dingmao, his son Guang Ying was established as crown prince; on gengwu an edict announced this inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingmao, his son Guang Ying was installed as crown prince; on gengwu an edict proclaimed it through the realm.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，如燕京。

translations.literal: On jiaxu he went to Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu he set out for Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 昭義軍節度使蕭仲宣家奴告其主怨謗。

translations.literal: A household slave of Xiao Zhongxuan, military commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army, accused his master of resentful slander.
translations.idiomatic: A bondservant of Xiao Zhongxuan, military commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army, denounced his master for seditious talk.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「仲宣之侄迪輦阿不近以誹謗誅，故敢妄訴。

translations.literal: The emperor said: “Zhongxuan’s nephew Dilian A’bu was lately executed for slander—that is why this fellow dares bring a false charge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “Zhongxuan’s nephew Dilian A’bu was just put to death for slander—no wonder this slave dares lodge a lying complaint.

sentences.zh: 」命殺告者。

translations.literal: ” He ordered the accuser killed.
translations.idiomatic: ” He had the informant executed.

sentences.zh: 迪輦阿不者，蕭拱也。

translations.literal: Dilian A’bu was Xiao Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Dilian A’bu was Xiao Gong.

sentences.zh: 戊子，次泰州。

translations.literal: On wuzi he halted at Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi he made camp at Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 三月丙申朔，以刑部尚書田秀穎等爲宋生日使。

translations.literal: Third month, on bingshen, new-moon day, Minister of Punishments Tian Xiuying and others were made envoys for Song’s imperial birthday.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingshen, the new moon, Minister of Punishments Tian Xiuying and others were sent as envoys for the Song emperor’s birthday.

sentences.zh: 四月丙寅朔，有司請今歲河南、北選人並赴中京銓注，從之。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on bingyin, new-moon day, the authorities asked that this year’s examination candidates from south and north of the Yellow River all attend civil appointment at the Central Capital; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on bingyin, the new moon, the ministries asked that candidates from both sides of the Yellow River come to the Central Capital for appointment that year; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，上自泰州如涼陘。

translations.literal: On renchen the emperor went from Taizhou to Liang Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he traveled from Taizhou to Liang Gorge.

sentences.zh: 五月丁酉，獵于立列只山。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on dingyou, he hunted on Mount Lieliezhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingyou, he hunted on Mount Lieliezhi.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，賜獵士，人一羊。

translations.literal: On jiayin each huntsman was given one sheep.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin each man of the hunt was given a sheep.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，次臨潢府。

translations.literal: On yimao he halted at Linhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao he halted at Linhuang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，太白經天。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Venus crossed the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Venus crossed the sky again.

sentences.zh: 六月甲子朔，駐綿山。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on jiazi, new-moon day, he encamped at Cotton Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiazi, the new moon, he encamped at Cotton Mountain.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，權楚底部猛安那野伏誅。

translations.literal: On wuyin Nayeqi, acting meng’an of the Chudi tribe, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Nayeqi, acting meng’an of the Chudi tribe, was put to death.

sentences.zh: 七月癸卯，命崇義軍節度使烏帶之妻唐括定哥殺其夫而納之。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on guimao, he ordered Tangguo Dingge, wife of Wudai, military commissioner of the Chongyi Army, to kill her husband, then took her into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on guimao, he ordered Tangguo Dingge, wife of Wudai, military commissioner of the Chongyi Army, to murder her husband, then brought her into the palace.

sentences.zh: 八月癸亥朔，獵于途你山。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on guihai, new-moon day, he hunted on Mount Tuni.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guihai, the new moon, he hunted on Mount Tuni.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以侍御史保魯鞫事不實，杖之。

translations.literal: On jiaxu the investigating censor Baolu was flogged because his inquiry did not match the facts.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the investigating censor Baolu was beaten for a prosecution that would not hold.

sentences.zh: 丙子，次于鐸瓦。

translations.literal: On bingzi he halted at Duowa.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi he halted at Duowa.

sentences.zh: 九月甲午，次中京。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on jiawu, he halted at the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiawu, he reached the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 丙午，尚書右丞相大抃罷。

translations.literal: On bingwu Right Director of the Secretariat Da Fen was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu right director of the secretariat Da Fen was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 殺太府少監劉景。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury Liu Jing was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jing, vice director of the imperial treasury, was executed.

sentences.zh: 以都水使者完顏麻潑爲高麗生日使，吏部郎中蕭中立爲夏國生日使。

translations.literal: Wanyan Mapo, commissioner of waterways, was made birthday envoy to Goryeo; Xiao Zhongli, bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel, was made birthday envoy to Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Mapo, commissioner of waterways, was sent as birthday envoy to Goryeo; Xiao Zhongli, a bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel, as birthday envoy to Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 十月壬戌朔，使使奉遷太廟神主。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on renxu, new-moon day, envoys were sent to convey and relocate the ancestral tablet spirits.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on renxu, the new moon, envoys were dispatched to move the spirit tablets of the imperial ancestors.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫趙資福罷。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhao Zifu was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Zhao Zifu was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以太子詹事張用直等爲賀宋正旦使。

translations.literal: On jiashen Zhang Yongzhi, steward of the Eastern Palace, and others were made envoys to congratulate Song on New Year’s Day.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Zhang Yongzhi, steward of the Eastern Palace, and others were sent to congratulate Song on New Year’s Day.

sentences.zh: 殺太祖長公主兀魯，杖罷其夫平章政事徒單恭，封其侍婢忽撻爲國夫人。

translations.literal: Taizu’s elder princess Wulu was killed; her husband, Grand Councilor Tudan Gong, was beaten and dismissed; her maid Huta was enfeoffed as State Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu’s elder princess Wulu was put to death; her husband, grand councilor Tudan Gong, was flogged and cashiered; her maid Huta was made State Lady.

sentences.zh: 恭之兄定哥初尚兀魯，定哥死，恭強納焉，而不相能，又與侍婢忽撻不協。

translations.literal: Gong’s elder brother Dingge had first married Wulu; after Dingge died, Gong forced her into his household, yet they could not live in accord, and he was also at odds with the maid Huta.
translations.idiomatic: Gong’s brother Dingge had first married Wulu; when Dingge died, Gong took her by force, yet husband and wife could not abide each other, and he quarreled with the maid Huta besides.

sentences.zh: 忽撻得幸于后，遂譖于上，故見殺，而並罷恭。

translations.literal: Huta won the empress’s favor and slandered Wulu to the emperor; hence Wulu was killed and Gong dismissed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Huta won the empress’s ear and poisoned the emperor against Wulu; Wulu died, and Gong was driven from office with her.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊戌，以咸平尹李德固爲平章政事。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on wuxu, Li Degu, intendant of Xianping, was made grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuxu, Li Degu, intendant of Xianping, was made grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，買珠于烏古迪烈部及蒲與路，禁百姓私相貿易，仍調兩路民夫，采珠一年。

translations.literal: Pearls were purchased from the Wugu Dilie tribe and Puyu Route; private trade among the people was forbidden, and corvée from both routes was levied to gather pearls for a year.
translations.idiomatic: The court bought pearls from the Wugu Dilie tribe and Puyu Route, forbade private dealing among commoners, and drafted labor from both routes to dive for pearls for a full year.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以前平章政事徒單恭爲司徒。

translations.literal: On wushen former Grand Councilor Tudan Gong was made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen former grand councilor Tudan Gong was made minister of education.

sentences.zh: 二月庚申，上自中京如燕京。

translations.literal: Second month, on gengshen, the emperor went from the Central Capital to Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengshen, the emperor left the Central Capital for Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 三月辛亥，上至燕京，初備法駕，甲寅，親選良家子百三十餘人充后宮。

translations.literal: Third month, on xinhai, he reached Yanjing, first equipped the full imperial train; on jiayin he personally selected more than a hundred and thirty daughters of good families for the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinhai, he entered Yanjing and for the first time marshaled the full imperial escort; on jiayin he chose in person more than a hundred and thirty daughters of respectable houses for the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以遷都詔中外。

translations.literal: On yimao an edict on moving the capital was proclaimed inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao an edict announcing the transfer of the capital was sent through the realm.

sentences.zh: 改元貞元。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The reign was retitled Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 改燕京爲中都，府曰大興，汴京爲南京，中京爲北京。

translations.literal: Yanjing was renamed the Central Capital, its prefecture called Daxing; Bian became the Southern Capital and the former Central Capital became the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjing became the Central Capital, its prefecture Daxing; Bian was made the Southern Capital and the old Central Capital the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以司徒徒單恭爲太保、領三省事，平章政事蕭裕爲右丞相兼中書令，右丞張浩、左丞張通古爲平章政事，參知政事張中孚爲左丞，蕭玉爲右丞，平章政事李德固爲司空，左宣徽使劉萼爲參知政事，樞密副使昂爲樞密使，工部尚書僕散師恭爲樞密副使。

translations.literal: On bingchen Tudan Gong, Minister of Education, was made Grand Guardian and head of the Three Departments; Grand Councilor Xiao Yu was made right director of the Secretariat and concurrently director of the Zhongshu office; Right Vice Director Zhang Hao and Left Vice Director Zhang Tonggu were made grand councilors; Participation Councillor Zhang Zhongfu was made left vice director; Xiao Yu was made right vice director; Grand Councilor Li Degu was made Minister of Works; Left Commissioner of the Palace Attendants’ Office Liu E was made participation councillor; Vice Privy Commissioner Ang was made privy commissioner; Minister of Works Pusan Shigong was made vice privy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Tudan Gong, minister of education, became grand guardian and head of the Three Departments; grand councilor Xiao Yu became right director of the secretariat and director of the Zhongshu office; right vice director Zhang Hao and left vice director Zhang Tonggu became grand councilors; participation councillor Zhang Zhongfu became left vice director; Xiao Yu became right vice director; grand councilor Li Degu became minister of works; left commissioner of the palace attendants’ office Liu E became participation councillor; vice privy commissioner Ang became privy commissioner; Minister of Works Pusan Shigong became vice privy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四月辛酉，以右宣徽使紇石烈撒合輦等爲賀宋生日使。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on xinyou, Right Xuanhui Commissioner Heshenlie Sahelian and others were made envoys to congratulate Song on the emperor’s birthday.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on xinyou, Heshenlie Sahelian, right commissioner of the Xuanhui Bureau, and others were sent as birthday envoys to Song.

sentences.zh: 辛未，特封唐括定哥爲貴妃。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Tangguo Dingge was specially ennobled as Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Tangguo Dingge was raised to Noble Consort by special decree.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，皇太后大氏崩。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Grand Empress Dowager of the Da clan died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the grand empress dowager of the Da clan died.

sentences.zh: 五月辛卯，殺弟西京留守蒲家。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on xinmao, the emperor killed his younger brother Pujia, regent at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinmao, he executed his younger brother Pujia, who held the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 西京兵馬完顏謨盧瓦、編修官圓福奴、通進孛迭坐與蒲家善，並殺之。

translations.literal: Wanyan Moluwa, Western Capital army commander; Yuanfunu, reviser; and Bediezuo, channel clerk—all were on good terms with Pujia and were killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Moluwa, commander of Western Capital forces; Yuanfunu, reviser; and Bediezuo, channel clerk—friends of Pujia—were put to death with him.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以京城隙地賜朝官及衛士。

translations.literal: On yimao, vacant plots in the capital were granted to court officials and guards.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao vacant land in the capital was handed out to officials and guardsmen.

sentences.zh: 六月乙丑，以安國軍節度使耶律恕爲參知政事。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on yichou, Yelu Shu, military commissioner of the Anguo Army, was made participation councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yichou, Yelu Shu, military commissioner of the Anguo Army, was named participation councillor.

sentences.zh: 七月戊子朔，元賜朝官京城隙地，征錢有差。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on wuzi, new-moon day, on the vacant capital land granted earlier to officials, money was levied in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the seventh month’s new moon, officials were charged graded fees for the capital plots they had received.

sentences.zh: 八月壬戌，司空李德固薨。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on renxu, Minister of Works Li Degu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renxu, Minister of Works Li Degu died.

sentences.zh: 禁中都路捕射麞兔。

translations.literal: Hunting deer and hares in the Central Capital circuit was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Deer and hare hunting in the Central Capital circuit was banned.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，賜營建宮室工匠及役夫帛。

translations.literal: On wuyin, cloth was bestowed on craftsmen and corvée laborers building the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin cloth was issued to the artisans and laborers raising the palace.

sentences.zh: 九月丁亥朔，以翰林待制謀良虎爲夏國生日使，吏部郎中窊合山爲高麗生日使。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on dinghai, new-moon day, Hanlin attendant drafting Moulianghu was made birthday envoy to Western Xia; Wahéshan, director in the Ministry of Personnel, was made birthday envoy to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the ninth month’s new moon, Moulianghu, Hanlin attendant drafting, was sent as birthday envoy to Western Xia; Wahéshan, a director in the Ministry of Personnel, as birthday envoy to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 十月丁巳，獵于良鄉。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on dingsi, he hunted at Liangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on dingsi, he hunted at Liangxiang.

sentences.zh: 封料石岡神爲靈應王。

translations.literal: The spirit of Liaoshigang was enfeoffed as Spirit-Responsive King.
translations.idiomatic: The deity of Liaoshigang was enfeoffed as Spirit-Responsive King.

sentences.zh: 初，海陵嘗過此祠，持杯珓禱曰：「使吾有天命，當得吉卜。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hailing had passed this shrine, he held a cup and cast divination blocks, praying: “If Heaven has granted me the Mandate, let the omen be auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Years before, passing the shrine, Hailing had raised a cup and cast divination blocks: “If the Mandate is truly mine, give me a lucky sign.

sentences.zh: 」投之，吉。

translations.literal: ” He cast them; the answer was auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: ” He threw them; the answer was lucky.

sentences.zh: 又禱曰：「果如所卜，他日當有報，否則毀爾祠宇。

translations.literal: He prayed again: “If the divination proves true, I shall repay you; if not, I will tear down your shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He prayed again: “If the omen holds, I will repay you; if not, I will raze your temple.

sentences.zh: 」投之，又吉，故封之。

translations.literal: ” He cast again; again auspicious—hence the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: ” He cast once more; again the sign was good—hence this enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 戊午，還宮。

translations.literal: On wuwu, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，有司言：「太后園陵未畢，合停冬享及祫祭。

translations.literal: On renxu the authorities reported: “The empress dowager’s park tomb is not yet finished; winter offerings and the collective ancestral rite ought to be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the ministries reported, “The empress dowager’s tomb park is unfinished; winter sacrifices and the collective rite should be postponed.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: ” The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙子，命內外官聞大功以上喪，止給當日假，若父母喪，聽給假三日，著爲令。

translations.literal: On bingzi an order was issued: officials who heard of a death within the greater-mourning grades were granted only the day’s leave; if a parent died, three days’ leave was allowed—this was made statute.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi it was decreed that when an official learned of a death among kin in the greater-mourning grades he received only that day’s leave; for a parent’s death, three days—and the rule was written into law.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙戌朔，定州獻嘉禾，詔自今不得復進。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on bingxu, new-moon day, Ding Prefecture presented auspicious grain; an edict forbade such submissions from now on.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, the eleventh month’s new moon, Ding Prefecture sent auspicious grain; an edict barred further such tributes.

sentences.zh: 己丑，瑤池殿成。

translations.literal: On jichou, Yaochi Hall was completed.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the Yaochi Hall was finished.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以戶部尚書蔡松年等爲賀宋正旦使。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Minister of Revenue Cai Songnian and others were made envoys to congratulate Song on New Year’s Day.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Cai Songnian, minister of revenue, and others were sent as Song New Year envoys.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，左丞相耨碗溫都思忠致仕。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Left Grand Councilor Wendusi Zhong retired.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Wendusi Zhong, left grand councilor, retired from office.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以樞密使昂爲左丞相，樞密副使僕散思恭爲樞密使。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Privy Commissioner Ang was made left grand councilor; Vice Privy Commissioner Pusan Sigong was made privy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Privy Commissioner Ang became left grand councilor; Vice Privy Commissioner Pusan Sigong became privy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十二月，太白經天。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Venus crossed the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Venus crossed the sky—an omen.

sentences.zh: 戊午，特賜貴妃唐括定哥家奴孫梅進士及第。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Sun Mei, a household slave of Noble Consort Tangguo Dingge, was specially granted passage of the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Sun Mei, a bondservant in Noble Consort Tangguo Dingge’s household, was specially passed in the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以簽書樞密院事南撒爲樞密副使。

translations.literal: On renxu, Nansa, acting privy commissioner, was made vice privy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Nansa, acting privy commissioner, was made vice privy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 辛未，對所納皇叔曹國王宗敏妃阿懶爲昭妃。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Alian, consort presented by his uncle Prince Zongmin of Cao, was made Illustrious Consort.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Alian, whom his uncle Prince Zongmin of Cao had offered him, was raised to Illustrious Consort.

sentences.zh: 丙子，貴妃唐括定哥坐與舊奴奸，賜死。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Noble Consort Tangguo Dingge, for adultery with a former slave, was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Noble Consort Tangguo Dingge was executed for sleeping with an old bondservant.

sentences.zh: 閏月乙酉朔，殺護衛特謨葛。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, on yiyou, new-moon day, the guard Temuge was killed.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the intercalary month’s new moon, the guardsman Temuge was executed.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，定社稷制度。

translations.literal: On guisi, the state-altar system was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the rites of the state altars were codified.

sentences.zh: 太白經天。

translations.literal: Venus crossed the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: Venus crossed the sky again.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，乙太保、領三省事徒單恭爲太保、領三省事如故。

translations.literal: On guimao, Grand Guardian Tudan Gong, who headed the Three Departments, was made grand guardian and head of the Three Departments as before.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Grand Guardian Tudan Gong, head of the Three Departments, was confirmed in those posts.

sentences.zh: 命西京路統軍撻懶、西北路招討蕭懷忠、臨潢府總管馬和尚、烏古迪烈司招討斜野等北巡。

translations.literal: An order sent Western Capital Route commander-in-chief Tadan, Northwestern Route pacification commissioner Xiao Huaizhong, Linhuang prefect Ma Heshang, and Ugu Dilie Route pacification commissioner Xieye and others on a northern inspection tour.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Western Capital Route commander Tadan, Northwestern Route pacification commissioner Xiao Huaizhong, Linhuang prefect Ma Heshang, and Ugu Dilie Route pacification commissioner Xieye, among others, to make a northern inspection.

sentences.zh: 二年正月甲寅朔，上不豫，不視朝。

translations.literal: Second year, first month, on jiayin, new-moon day, the emperor was ill and held no court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on jiayin, the first month’s new moon, the emperor fell ill and did not hold audience.

sentences.zh: 賜宋、高麗、夏使就館燕。

translations.literal: Song, Goryeo, and Xia envoys were feasted at their lodgings.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from Song, Goryeo, and Western Xia were entertained in their quarters.

sentences.zh: 庚申，太白經天。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Venus crossed the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Venus crossed the sky again.

sentences.zh: 尚書右丞相蕭裕與前真定尹蕭馮家奴、前御史中丞蕭招折、博州同知遙設等謀反，伏誅，詔中外。

translations.literal: Right Grand Councilor Xiao Yu, with the former bondservant of former Zhending prefect Xiao Feng, former censor-in-chief Xiao Zhaozhe, and Bozhou vice commissioner Yaoshe, plotted rebellion; they were executed, and an edict announced this within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Right Grand Councilor Xiao Yu conspired with a former slave of ex-prefect Xiao Feng of Zhending, former censor-in-chief Xiao Zhaozhe, and Bozhou vice commissioner Yaoshe; all were put to death, and an edict proclaimed it through the realm.

sentences.zh: 己巳，生辰，宋、高麗、夏遣使來賀。

translations.literal: On jisi, his birthday; Song, Goryeo, and Xia sent envoys to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, his birthday, Song, Goryeo, and Western Xia sent congratulatory envoys.

sentences.zh: 二月甲申朔，以平章政事張浩爲尚書右丞相兼中書令。

translations.literal: Second month, on jiashen, new-moon day, Participation Councillor Zhang Hao was made right grand councilor and concurrently director of the Zhongshu office.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the second month’s new moon, Participation Councillor Zhang Hao became right grand councilor and director of the Zhongshu office.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以尚書右丞蕭玉爲平章政事，前河南路統軍使張輝爲尚書右丞，西北路招討使蕭好胡爲樞密副使。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Right Vice Director Xiao Yu was made participation councillor; former Henan Route commander-in-chief Zhang Hui was made right vice director; Northwestern Route pacification commissioner Xiao Haohu was made vice privy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Right Vice Director Xiao Yu became participation councillor; former Henan Route commander Zhang Hui became right vice director; and Northwestern Route pacification commissioner Xiao Haohu became vice privy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三月戊辰，夏遣使賀遷都。

translations.literal: Third month, on wuchen, Xia sent envoys to congratulate the transfer of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuchen, Western Xia sent envoys to congratulate the move of the capital.

sentences.zh: 四月丙戌，幸大興府及都轉運使司。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on bingxu, he visited Daxing Prefecture and the metropolitan transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on bingxu, he inspected Daxing Prefecture and the metropolitan transport office.

sentences.zh: 遣薦含桃于衍慶宮。

translations.literal: Cherries were sent as offerings to Yanging Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Cherries were sent as offerings to Yanging Palace.

sentences.zh: 五月癸丑朔，日有食之，避正殿，敕百官勿治事。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on guichou, new-moon day, there was a solar eclipse; he avoided the main hall and ordered the hundred officials not to conduct business.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, the fifth month’s new moon, an eclipse fell; he left the main hall and commanded officials to suspend business.

sentences.zh: 己未，詔自今每月上七日不奏刑名，尚食進饌不進肉。

translations.literal: On jiwei, an edict ordered that for the first seven days of each month criminal cases were not to be reported, and the imperial kitchen was not to serve meat in the emperor’s meals.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei an edict barred criminal reports during the first seven days of every month and forbade meat in the emperor’s table for those days.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，始置交鈔庫，設使副員。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the jiaochao treasury was first established, with commissioner and vice commissioner posts.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the paper-note treasury was founded for the first time, with commissioner and deputy posts.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，太原尹徒單阿里出虎伏誅，復命其子朮斯剌乘傳焚其骨，擲水中。

translations.literal: On dingchou Tudan Ali Chuhu, prefect of Taiyuan, was put to death in secret; then his son Shisila was ordered to travel by post relay, burn the bones, and cast them into the water.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Tudan Ali Chuhu, prefect of Taiyuan, was secretly executed; the court then sent his son Shisila by relay post to burn the bones and throw them into a river.

sentences.zh: 七月庚申，初設鹽鈔香茶文引印造庫使副。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on gengshen, commissioners were first appointed for the office that printed salt certificates, incense-tea passes, and document warrants.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on gengshen, the court first set up commissioners for printing salt notes, incense-and-tea warrants, and official passes.

sentences.zh: 丙子，參知政事耶律恕罷。

translations.literal: On bingzi Participation Councillor Yelü Shu was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi participation councillor Yelü Shu left office.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊辰，上命諸從姊妹皆分屬諸妃，出入禁中，與爲淫亂，臥內遍設地衣，裸逐爲戲。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on wuchen, the emperor ordered all his paternal cousins assigned to various consorts; they entered the inner palace and debauched with them. The sleeping chambers were lined with floor mats, and they ran about naked in sport.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuchen, the emperor assigned every paternal cousin to a consort’s household so they could enter the inner palace for orgies; the bedchambers were carpeted wall to wall, and the kin ran naked in chase as sport.

sentences.zh: 是月，初置惠民局。

translations.literal: That month the Beneficence Pharmacy was first established.
translations.idiomatic: That month the court opened the Beneficence Pharmacy for public medicine.

sentences.zh: 高麗遣使謝賜生日。

translations.literal: Goryeo sent envoys to thank the court for birthday gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo sent envoys to thank the throne for birthday largesse.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙酉，乙太傅溫都思忠爲太師，領三省事如故，平章政事張通古爲司徒，平章政事如故。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on yiyou, Grand Tutor Wendusi Zhong was made Grand Preceptor, head of the Three Departments as before; Grand Councilor Zhang Tonggu was made Minister of Education, grand councilor as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yiyou, grand tutor Wendusi Zhong became grand preceptor and still headed the Three Departments; grand councilor Zhang Tonggu became minister of education while keeping his council seat.

sentences.zh: 三年正月己酉朔，宋、高麗、夏遣使來賀。

translations.literal: Third year, first month, on jiyou, new-moon day, Song, Goryeo, and Xia sent envoys to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on jiyou, the first month’s new moon, Song, Goryeo, and Western Xia sent New Year envoys.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以判東京留守大抃爲太傅、領三省事。

translations.literal: On xinyou the former Eastern Capital regent Da Fen was made Grand Tutor and head of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Da Fen, who had governed the Eastern Capital, was made grand tutor and head of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 甲子，生辰，宋、高麗、夏遣使來賀。

translations.literal: On jiazi, his birthday; Song, Goryeo, and Xia sent envoys to congratulate.
